requirement:
When loading a supported legacy evidence record that did not capture its
procedure version, Habeas Codicem represents that missing version as `*`.
In-place conversion preserves this wildcard rather than assigning the current
version. The wildcard matches any
requested review revision under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.procedure_match`.
The record is current when its recorded inputs and all existing application
freshness checks still match. Version matching leaves the subject, reference-set,
input, determination, citation, and site checks intact.

For new assessments, Habeas Codicem's validation value supplies a concrete review revision
other than `*`, and the assessment records it.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate. I did not request implementation source. I mapped each obligation in `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.legacy_freshness` to a test, as follows.

- **Legacy load represents the missing version as `*`.**
  - `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[legacy_conversion_preserves_every_historical_field_without_resolving_sources]` decodes legacy requirement, example, citation and site records. It asserts `record.revision == "*"`.
  - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once]` loads the legacy file through `load_evidence` for all four subject kinds. It asserts `loaded.revision == "*"`.

- **In-place conversion preserves the wildcard instead of assigning the current version.**
  - `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[legacy_conversion_preserves_every_historical_field_without_resolving_sources]` asserts `encode` writes `review_version == "*"` and that `view(&native)` equals the old record.
  - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[current_legacy_authoring_converts_without_configuration_and_stdout_never_converts]` runs the real in-place conversion on a legacy file. It asserts the written `review_version` is `"*"` and the historical view is unchanged.
  - The semantic-mutation loop in `every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once` also asserts `native["review_version"] == "*"`.

- **The wildcard matches any requested revision.** `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[native_freshness_checks_versions_inputs_and_application_fields]` asserts a `*` record is current for `"future-review-version"`. In the same test, a `*` record is checked against `"any"` and fails there only because the input text changed. A concrete mismatch (`old-concrete-version` against `REVIEW_VERSION`) is not current. That shows the wildcard is not treated as a general pass.

- **The record is current when inputs and application checks still match.** In `every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once`, an unmodified legacy record and its native `*` or concrete-version form produce no findings. Both forms give identical findings.

- **Version matching leaves the subject, reference-set, input, determination, citation and site checks intact.**
  - Each of these is mutated on a `*` record in the semantic-mutation loop. The mutations are determination false, changed inputs, changed subject text, changed reference-set hash, citation file, item and commentary, and site requirement, file, item, queries, fixmes and `applies` false.
  - The test asserts that the legacy findings contain the expected message. It then asserts the converted native `*` record gives identical findings. Staleness is not turned into a load error.
  - Each of these mutations is rejected while the version is `*`, so a wildcard cannot bypass them. The input-change case is also covered at the graph level by `native_freshness_checks_versions_inputs_and_application_fields`.

- **New assessments record a concrete revision other than `*`.** `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[authoring_keeps_the_prepared_subject_snapshot_and_concrete_version]` asserts `review_version == REVIEW_VERSION` and `!= "*"`. It also checks that the decoded record is stale against the changed project, so a concrete version does not make a record match by itself.

The wildcard-only-for-complete-`*` rule belongs to the cited `procedure_match` requirement. Under the task rules, that cited requirement needs no reassessment here. The tests carry the correct `{test}` markings for the subject, so there is no marking gap. I found no gaps and no applicable {fixme} acknowledgments.

// Defined in trust_but_verify.
/// Compare the saved review-rule revision with the currently requested revision.
pub fn procedure_matches(stored: &str, requested: &str) -> bool;
The revision matches when the stored `Record::revision` is `*` or equals the
requested revision exactly. Only the complete stored value `*` is a wildcard;
other values compare literally. A wildcard leaves dependency comparison and
result decoding unchanged. It matches revisions for the selected source and
criterion only, and does not supply evidence for other criteria.
